shared-needs.text: Declared, not linked: the shared author writes these volumes and anchors; check.sh matches each need against shared/ when it lands. Nothing below points at a file that does not exist in this pull request.
shared-needs.need: 201 accepted or passed: ticket, ticket-set.accepted, review.passed; acts: N-03 or N-09
400 bad record: validator.refused schema; acts: N-11, plus a defect on N-15 when two schema checks disagree
422 rejected with evidence: review.changes, validator.refused with the check and the command; acts: N-11
500 failed after 3 or a defect: seat.bundle.failed, workspace.failed, phase.failed, validator.failed, launcher.defect; acts: N-11, or N-06 health then N-28 for a defect
tickets: the whole ticket as a record (files, acceptance with observed_exit_on_main, depends_on, status, set_id); retention by N-45
ticket_sets: ticket-set.draft and ticket-set.accepted by set_id with anchor, repo_sha, attempt, verdict_ref
id_mint: reserved ids unique on (set_id, key) and on id, so a crashed mint resumes with the same ids
record kinds registry: every record kind with its code set, writer node and schema path, loaded by N-43 with the code table; test.proof registered for dark builds
one concern, a few files (at most 6), a diff a reviewer reads in minutes; when in doubt split
D11: validation, close-out, merge, cleanup and record puts are code with tests; an LLM writes, judges or rules

section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-18 is code that decides whether a drafted ticket may exist. It runs every acceptance command on main and records the observed exit code, refuses a ticket whose acceptance cannot run, whose files are undeclared or overlap inside the set, whose input and output records are not declared, or whose size breaks the small-ticket rule, and mints ids only for tickets that pass. Nothing an LLM wrote becomes a ticket until this node has run it (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#18-d16-may-an-llm-decompose-work-into-tickets option B).

The rule it enforces was written in rime as R3 and never built: "The architect runs every acceptance command against origin/main before a ticket is cut and records the observed exit code in the ticket. A ticket whose acceptance cannot be run is not cut" (rebuild/investigation/L09-earlier-factory-iterations.md#7-decisions-an-llm-makes-that-a-rule-could-make); five of seven supersedes in that iteration were acceptance that could not be satisfied. Here it is a function with a test.

section.title: Input record: ticket-set.draft
section.text: Kind ticket-set.draft, code 100, from N-17; schema ../N-17/record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket-set.draft. The node reads set_id, anchor, repo_sha, tickets and verdict_ref.

section.title: Output records: ticket (accepted) and ticket-set.accepted, or validator.refused
section.text: On a pass, one ticket record per drafted ticket, kind ticket, code 201, with a minted id WO-<yyyymmdd>-<4 hex> (the existing id shape, minted from the store's id_mint table so two sets cannot take one id; bin/mint-id.sh carried into the store), every drafted field, acceptance[].observed_exit_on_main and observed_at and log_path, depends_on resolved to ids, status cut, set_id, idempotency_key set_id plus key. Then one ticket-set.accepted, code 201, listing the ids. The ticket records are the input of N-03 (re-entry, ../../dag.md#4-re-entries). Each acceptance entry keeps proves, the checklist item of the node volume the command proves (as N-17 drafted it, checked by C3 to exist), and the record names source_request when the set was cut from a cut request (nodes/N-03/spec.xml#input), so N-03 closes that request when the set is accepted; the checklist.state view reads proves (nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views), which makes this node one of the writers behind the Machine screen's checklist panel.

On a refusal, one validator.refused, code 422 (a check failed with evidence) or 400 (the draft failed its schema), idempotency_key set_id, with the failing ticket key, the check name, the command, the observed exit, the stderr tail and the log path. A refusal refuses the whole set: tickets are cut together or not at all, so a set's depends_on never dangles. Nothing is minted on a refusal.
Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket, ticket-set.accepted, validator.refused.

section.title: Mechanism: the checks, in order
section.text: Package scheduler/internal/validator. Validate(ctx, draft) runs the checks below in order and stops at the first failure; the order puts the cheap and deterministic checks before the one that runs commands. Every check writes one line to the set's validate.log with its name, result and duration.
section.step: Schema: the draft validates against ../N-17/record.schema.json (the launcher checked the seat's output; this is the record check, the same file).
Anchor: git -C mirror rev-list -1 origin/main -- <anchor volume path> must not be newer than draft.repo_sha; else anchor_moved, because the author read an older design.

Files: every ticket has at least one file; no path is an aggregate (CHANGELOG.md, work-orders/INDEX.md, CONTEXT_STATE.md, README files that are generated) or a runtime path (events/, logs/, anything under the state root); the overlap rule of factory/bin/claims.sh across the tickets of the set finds no pair; count at most seats.json ticket_max_files (default 6); every path pattern matches at least one existing path on main or names a new file under an existing directory (a typo is refused, not discovered by a worker).

Records: input_record and output_record name kinds in the record kinds registry (a shared need of section shared-needs, loaded by N-43 with the code table); a dark build's output may be test.proof, a registered kind for exactly this case.

Depends: keys resolve inside the set, ids exist in the store with a status that is not cancelled or dead, and the graph of set plus existing tickets is acyclic (Kahn's algorithm); a go_live ticket depends on its build ticket.

Size: files.count equals len(files); diff_lines_estimate at most seats.json ticket_max_diff_lines (default 600); concern is one sentence (no "and" joining two verbs is a heuristic the check does not attempt; the reviewer judges concern; the validator checks the counts).

Duplicate: no accepted ticket (status cut, ready, started, or with an open pull request) on the same node with the same file set and the same acceptance commands; a duplicate is refused naming the existing id and title.

Mint and put in one store transaction: reserve ids in id_mint for (set_id, key) with a unique index so a retry after a crash returns the same ids; put every ticket record with idempotency_key set_id:key; put ticket-set.accepted with idempotency_key set_id. A partial transaction never shows: the store commits all or none.

section.title: Running the acceptance commands on main
section.text: The validator borrows a read-only verify workspace from N-14 (Provision with role validator, base_ref origin/main, no claims) and runs every acceptance command of every ticket in the set, each as one container from the pinned test image (ci/images.json, N-22) with the workspace mounted read-only at /work, no network, no service account, a cpu and memory limit from seats.json validator_container, and a timeout of the command's timeout_seconds (default 300). Why a container and not the host shell: the gate (N-24) runs the same commands in pods from the same image, so the exit the validator observes is the exit the gate will observe; a host run would observe the host's tools. Why not a pod in slice one: the validator needs the exit code within a minute and the cluster round trip is a later ticket; the container is the host's podman with the same image digest, and moving C7 into N-24 is a one-line change of the executor verb once the pod path is measured.
What the check records: observed_exit_on_main, duration, stdout and stderr tails (2000 bytes), log_path. What the check refuses:
section.rule: exit 126 or 127 (not executable, command not found), a timeout, a make target that does not exist (make reports "No rule to make target"), or a script path that does not exist on main. The ticket asked for a proof that cannot be produced.

observed exit equals expect_exit and regression_guard is false. A command that already passes on main proves nothing about the change; the author must name a command that flips, or mark it a regression guard (which is allowed, and recorded as such, so the reviewer knows it proves no new behaviour).

runs_in is pod and the command's suite is not in the suite planner's map (N-23 suites.json); an unmapped path plans the full set at the gate, which is sound, but a ticket must name its suite so the proof is readable.
section.text: What the check accepts and records: a non-zero exit that is a real failure (the test exists and fails on main because the feature is not built) with the exit code; a regression guard that passes. Observed exits ride on the ticket so the worker's brief (N-13) shows them, the reviewer (N-19) compares them with the evidence, and the gate's flip from observed to expected is the proof.

The commands run in parallel up to seats.json validator_parallel (default 4) with the total bounded by the sum of timeouts divided by the parallelism; the whole C7 step has a bound of seats.json validator_total_seconds (default 1800); past it the set is refused with validator_timeout naming the commands still running, and the author's next attempt must shrink or split.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: The validator controller (N-06 unit) is level-triggered on every tick: it lists ticket-set.draft records with no ticket-set.accepted and no validator.refused for the set_id and validates each. A draft is the only trigger; there is no approve verb, no stamp, no architect. A re-validation of an already-judged set never happens (the records exist), so a replayed draft is a no-op.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.what: store reads and the mint transaction
wait.fallback: validator.failed 500 store_unreachable; the next tick retries the set (nothing was minted)
validator.failed 500 workspace; the next tick retries

wait.timeout: timeout_seconds of the command, default 300, max 1800
wait.attempts: 1 per command; an infrastructure failure of podman itself (image pull, daemon) is retried 3 times with 10 s, 30 s, 90 s, an exit of the command is never retried (V05)
wait.fallback: cannot_run refusal for a timeout; validator.failed 500 for podman after 3
validator.refused 422 validator_timeout naming the running commands

wait.what: image pull of the pinned test image
wait.fallback: validator.failed 500 image; N-22 is the owner of the image and its digest pin is the fix

section.text: Bound per set: about 40 minutes in the worst case; no wait depends on a person.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: A validator.refused is the author's failure: N-11 dispatches a spec-author attempt n+1 with the refusal attached (N-17 retries section); after 3 the anchor is dead for cutting and one card is posted. A validator.failed 500 (infrastructure: store, workspace, podman, image) is the validator's own failure: the next tick retries the same set up to 3 times with 30 s, 60 s, 120 s; then a validator.failed with attempts 3 is a defect record and N-28 posts one card about the infrastructure, not about the draft. Recovery after a restart: the tick re-lists unjudged drafts; the mint reservation table makes a crashed M step resume with the same ids; a left-over verify workspace is released by N-14's cleanup of slots whose run has no live holder.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Many drafts validate at once, each in its own verify workspace and containers, in a pool of seats.json validator_workers (default 2, because each uses up to 4 containers). The repository on main is read-only to all of them.

Collision 1, two validations of one set (restart overlap): the mint reservation is unique on (set_id, key) and the puts are idempotent by set_id:key; the second pass commits nothing new; the second pass's containers are wasted work bounded by the timeouts, reported as a counter.

Collision 2, two sets accepted with overlapping files: allowed; files overlap across sets is a scheduling order that N-03 serializes by the claims rule; the validator refuses overlap only inside one set, where it is a cut defect.

Collision 3, two sets drafted from one anchor with duplicate tickets: C6 refuses the second set's duplicates naming the first set's ids; the second author's retry sees them in the existing tickets list.

Collision 4, main moves during C7: the commands ran at the verify workspace's base_sha, which is recorded on every ticket as observed_at_sha; the worker's branch is cut from a newer main (N-14), and that is fine: the observed exit is evidence of the command's runnability and baseline, not a promise about a sha; a command that stops running on a newer main surfaces at the gate as a red coq/gate with the command named.

Collision 5, the id mint under two validators: the store's id_mint table is the single sequence with a unique index on the id; a collision on the 4 hex suffix (date plus random) retries the random part up to 3 times inside the transaction.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: A ticket exists with its observed exits. Acts: N-03 (readiness).
The set is cut. Acts: N-03 reads the tickets; the Stats screen counts.
The draft failed its schema. Acts: N-11; a schema failure past the launcher's own check is also a defect record on N-15 (two checks of one schema disagreed).

A check failed with evidence: anchor_moved, files, records, depends, size, duplicate, acceptance (cannot_run, already_passing, runs_in_pod_unknown), validator_timeout. Acts: N-11 dispatches the author's next attempt with the record attached.
Infrastructure: store_unreachable, workspace, podman, image. Acts: the next tick, 3 times, then a card about the infrastructure.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.writes: validate.log, one <key>-<acceptance id>.log per command with argv, exit, duration, stdout and stderr
path.retention: 30 days after ticket-set.accepted or validator.refused; the ticket records carry the log_path, so a worker's brief can cite it while the ticket is live, and a live ticket's set is never cleaned

section.path: Dry run by default; --apply deletes; registered in N-45's scheduler/config/cleanup.json as validator-logs.

path.retention: released at the end of Validate; reclaimed by the slot expiry if Validate died

path.writes: container state under the host user's podman storage
path.cleanup: podman rm at the end of each command; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-validator.sh --containers removes any labelled container older than 1 hour

section.text: Tickets live in the store (table tickets); their retention is N-45's store retention (merged plus 90 days; cancelled or dead plus 30 days, after the card is answered). Nothing is written into the repository.

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The validator (Go service, host user): gRPC to the store; podman run with the pinned image, read-only mount, no network (--network none), no secrets, cpu and memory limits; read the mirror. No GitHub token, no cluster access, no write to any workspace.
No seat is involved: the validator is code. The spec-author cannot run the validator or read its logs before the record exists; the worker reads only the observed exits on its ticket.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/validator -run TestCannotRunRefused: a fixture draft with a command 'make no-such-target' yields validator.refused 422 acceptance cannot_run naming the command and exit 2

section.item: A command that cannot run on main refuses the set.

item.proof: go test TestAlreadyPassingRefused: a command that exits 0 on main with expect_exit 0 and regression_guard false yields already_passing; the same with regression_guard true is accepted and recorded

section.item: A passing command proves nothing unless named a guard.

item.proof: go test TestOverlapInsideSetRefused: two tickets in one set declaring line/bin/* and line/bin/merge.sh yields files refusal; two sets with the same overlap are both accepted

section.item: Overlap inside a set is a cut defect; across sets it is scheduling.

item.proof: go test TestCycleRefused: t1 depends on t2 and t2 on t1 yields depends refusal; a go_live ticket without its build dependency yields depends refusal

section.item: The dependency graph is acyclic and go-live follows build.

item.proof: go test TestMintIdempotent: Validate run twice on one set (the first crashed after the mint) yields the same ids and one ticket-set.accepted

section.item: A crashed mint resumes with the same ids.

item.proof: go test TestAllOrNothing: a set whose last ticket fails C7 mints nothing; the store shows no ticket for the set

section.item: A set is cut together or not at all.

item.proof: probe: a fixture draft with 4 commands of 10 s each runs C7 in under 25 s with validator_parallel 4; a command of 400 s with timeout 300 is refused cannot_run at 300 s

section.item: Commands run in parallel and are bounded.

item.proof: probe: the acceptance container cannot reach the network (curl to github.com fails) and cannot write /work (touch fails)

section.item: The container is hermetic and read-only.

item.proof: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-validator.sh --dry-run lists sets older than 30 days with no live ticket and keeps a set with a started ticket; --apply removes the first only

section.item: Cleanup keeps evidence of live tickets.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: sets_validated, sets_accepted, sets_refused_by_check, tickets_minted, acceptance_commands_run, acceptance_cannot_run, acceptance_already_passing, validate_seconds histogram, validator_failed_by_reason. The Stats screen (N-40) shows the refusal rate by check; the Alerts screen (N-41) shows validator.failed (infrastructure) and a cannot_run rate above seats.json cannot_run_alert (default 0.3 over 10 sets), because that means the brief template or the make targets drifted. The Machine screen (N-39) for N-18 shows sets in validation with the command currently running and its elapsed time.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See why a set was refused: the validator.refused record names the check and the command; the log is $COQ_STATE/validator/<set_id>/<key>-<a>.log.
A cannot_run on a real make target: the test image lacks a tool; the fix is N-22 (image config) and a ticket there, never a host run of the command to "prove" it.
Re-run a validation by hand: not a path; a set has one verdict. A changed draft is a new spec-author run (N-17) and a new set.
Infrastructure failed 3 times: the card names store, workspace, podman or image; after the fix the next tick revalidates the set without any hand step.
Cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-validator.sh [--apply] [--containers]; registered in N-45.

section.title: DAG edges in and out

edge.record: ticket records accepted enter intake as new tickets (../../dag.md#4-re-entries)

section.text: N-18 borrows a workspace from N-14 by a library call and the image digest from N-22's image record; neither is a drawn edge.

section.title: Sources cited
section.source: D16 option B: the validator's four checks
R3 and the unbuilt cut-check.sh; F-PL3 five of seven supersedes
D01 approve by rule: lint, files field, no contradicted node, evidence method per criterion, DAG input and output declared
F3 the stamp, F4 cut PRs
pod-per-case isolation and the pinned test image; infrastructure retried, assertions never
T04 a verdict the agent can read and cannot edit; T13 enforcement before the model call
set, start, diff, ids verbs: the files field, overlap rule, aggregate refusal, unique doc numbers
the id shape and uniqueness, carried into the store's mint table
the cut checklist: files declared, test plan runs through a repository target, no overlap
dequeue refuses a ticket whose depends_on is not done; carried to N-03, with the acyclic check here
tickets are small: one concern, a few files, a diff read in minutes; every node carries a checklist with proof
a node ships dark and goes live by its own ticket with a named proof
the graph tool's defect; the dependency graph is now rows in the store

item.what: an approval verb with a reason string
item.reason: L11 F3: a free-text field typed by an LLM and no check; the validator's checks replace it

item.what: a graph tool over ticket files
item.reason: depends_on is rows in the store; graph.sh truncated sources on ':' (memory graph-sh-source-colon-truncation)

item.what: banning greps over the ticket's code blocks
item.reason: never built; running the commands is the check

item.source: L13 D01 'graph.sh find shows no contradicted DEC node'
item.what: a contradiction check against decision nodes
item.reason: decisions are rulings in the store (N-29) and the spec book; a ticket cites an anchor, and anchor_moved catches a stale read; a semantic contradiction is the reviewer's judgement

item.what: a refused start as a 412 item back to the architect lane
item.reason: a refusal goes to N-11 and a fresh spec-author run; the architect hears about the third only, through a card
the validator is the mechanical half; the decomposition stays an LLM judgement (D16)
